correctness.rationale: The exact infinity norm formulas follow from (DM)^(-1)=M^(-1)D^(-1). Normalizing a maximal block by a common dyadic factor and monotonically enlarging every other admissible exponent yields one of b explicit candidates. The largest circular logarithmic gap gives a 2^(1-1/b) rounding guarantee; block-diagonal equally spaced binary-log entries prove equality for each b. All quantifiers, b=1 boundary, positive group norms, and unbounded integer exponents are covered. The standard-library checker passed 168 independent exact-rational matrices, 19558 exhaustive bounded exponent assignments, and 9 supplementary diagonal sharpness cases; those finite checks are not used as a proof of the universal claims.

originality.rationale: The first-public 2026 block-row mixed-precision source explicitly treats blockwise binary D and the factor kappa_infinity(DM), but offers no global discrete minimizer or block-count-sharp penalty. A 2003 full-text treatment solves classical unrestricted continuous two-sided p-norm scaling; it does not claim integer-exponent admissibility or the circular logarithm gap. LAPACK documents a bounded-radix heuristic with no guarantee of decreasing the condition number. The accessible abstract of Shapiro (1985) addresses block diagonal l2 scaling, not this dyadic infinity-norm classification. Four targeted published-record semantic searches, targeted web searches, and claims from the accessible earlier ledger found no equivalent or dominating theorem. Historical unindexed priority remains a real risk, so this is best-knowledge novelty, not proof of uniqueness.
residual_risks: Full text of Shapiro (1985) was not available for a decisive exclusion; its abstract, however, specifies the l2 norm.
Older literature on radix rounding, matrix balancing or logarithmic-circle dispersion might contain the exact theorem under different terminology.
Even when the condition-number factor is optimal, the full mixed-precision error bound can favor a different scaling.

value.rationale: The 2026 mixed-precision source identifies blockwise binary scaling as a meaningful error-control degree of freedom yet leaves the condition-number factor unoptimized. The result reduces an unbounded integer search to at most b explicit candidates and gives the sharp unavoidable performance loss against ideal real scaling, including extremal witnesses. These are natural conditioning design invariants, not arbitrary slices; the theorem carefully avoids unsupported claims about the entire solver error bound.
